key_insight: AlgoEvo turns automated algorithm discovery from a fixed search pipeline into a self-evolving agentic process. By letting an autonomous agent adapt its strategy using execution feedback, the system can reason more flexibly and accumulate knowledge across steps.
problem_solved: Existing algorithm-discovery frameworks rely on rigid, predefined control flows that limit adaptive reasoning, hinder transfer across search strategies, and waste useful feedback from code execution.
method: Uses a unified agentic framework that dynamically inspects the search process instead of following a fixed pipeline.
Accumulates and reuses knowledge from previous attempts and execution outcomes to guide future discovery steps.
Enables cross-paradigm transfer so the agent can adapt algorithm-search behavior rather than staying locked into one search pattern.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could make automated algorithm design more robust, flexible, and efficient. It may reduce manual tuning and help systems discover better solutions by learning from their own trial-and-error process.

paper_title: AlgoEvo: Self-Evolving Agentic Search for Automated Algorithm Discovery
paper_authors: Junhao Qiu, Qinglong Hu, Xialiang Tong, Mingxuan Yuan, Liyong Lin
